claim_1.claim: Luminex analysis of serum from 91 young and older individuals at baseline showed circulating IL-13 and IFN-γ cytokine levels were higher in young CMV+ individuals compared to young CMV− individuals.

sources.quote: In particular, we found an elevation of circulating IL-13 and IFN-γ cytokines, and higher CD8+ pSTAT1 and pSTAT3 responses to IL-6 in CMV+ individuals in the younger cohort compared to the CMV− subjects (Fig. 1).

Figure 1. Different immunological profiles in aging versus CMV seropositivity The contribution of age and CMV to immunological and gene expression profiles was estimated by a combination of nuclear norm and the Elastic net methods (see Methods). The magnitude of the regression coefficients used to separate the classes yCMV− and oCMV− (CMV-independent age effect) or yCMV− and yCMV+ (age-independent CMV effect) are shown in light and dark grey bars, respectively.

claim_3.claim: Whole blood microarray analysis of whole blood from 91 young and older individuals at baseline showed expression of module 103 and module 30 was elevated in young CMV+ individuals compared to young CMV− individuals.

sources.quote: At the gene expression level, the CMV effect independent of age was an up-regulation of genes associated with immune activation. For example, expression of module 103 (antigen processing and presentation, P < 0.00001 and NK cell mediated cytotoxicity, P < 0.00001) was elevated in yCMV+ (Fig. 1) and this module includes several KIR2 and KIR3 genes as well as GZMH (see http://cs.unc.edu/~vjojic/fluy2-upd/mod103.html), genes typically highly expressed in NK cells and in CD4+ and CD8+ T lacking CD28 (38, 39).. The expression of the gene module 30 was also elevated in yCMV+ (Fig. 1) and this module is composed of HLA-DOA and –DOB genes , which clustered with APOD, LAMC1, MIR600 among other genes.

Figure 1. Different immunological profiles in aging versus CMV seropositivity The contribution of age and CMV to immunological and gene expression profiles was estimated by a combination of nuclear norm and the Elastic net methods (see Methods). The magnitude of the regression coefficients used to separate the classes yCMV− and oCMV− (CMV-independent age effect) or yCMV− and yCMV+ (age-independent CMV effect) are shown in light and dark grey bars, respectively.

claim_4.claim: Whole blood microarray analysis of whole blood from 91 young and older individuals at baseline showed gene modules associated with cell cycle (module 34 and 101), protein synthesis (module 35 and 39), amino-acid metabolism (module 43), cell-death (modules 47 and 54), the ubiquitination pathway (module 98), HIF1α signaling (module 101), LXR/RXR activation (module 102), and the metabolism of carbohydrates (module 108) were down-regulated in older CMV− individuals compared to young CMV− individuals.

sources.quote: The age effect independent of CMV (yCMV− vs oCMV−) revealed down-regulation of several gene modules (Fig. 1) including those associated with cell cycle (module 34 and 101, P = 0.019), protein synthesis (module 35 and 39, P = 0.0009 and P < 0.0001, respectively) amino-acid metabolism (module 43, P = 0.0023), cell-death (modules 47 and 54, P = 0.0021 and P < 0.0001, respectively), the ubiquitination pathway (module 98, P = 0.0092), HIF1α signaling (module 101, P < 0.0001), LXR/RXR activation, which is involved in cholesterol and lipid metabolism (module 102, P = 0.007) and the metabolism of carbohydrates (module 108, P = 0.00074).

Figure 1. Different immunological profiles in aging versus CMV seropositivity The contribution of age and CMV to immunological and gene expression profiles was estimated by a combination of nuclear norm and the Elastic net methods (see Methods). The magnitude of the regression coefficients used to separate the classes yCMV− and oCMV− (CMV-independent age effect) or yCMV− and yCMV+ (age-independent CMV effect) are shown in light and dark grey bars, respectively.

claim_5.claim: Hemagglutinin-inhibition (HAI) assay analysis of serum from 30 young (20–30 years) and 61 older (60–>89 years) individuals at day 0 and 28±7 days after influenza vaccination (day 28) in year 1 showed the antibody response to trivalent inactivated influenza vaccination was lower in older individuals compared to young individuals.

sources.quote: As expected, a negative effect of age was observed in the antibody response to IIV (P < 0.0001) (Fig. 2a).

Figure 2. Young but not old CMV+ individuals have a better response to influenza vaccination The geometric mean titer (GMT) for all three strains in the vaccine was calculated for each individual in the study and a standardized score (delta (Δ) post-pre GMT) for response was computed as described in Methods (y-axis). A higher response is observed in yCMV+ compared to yCMV− in the first (a) and second (b) year, as well as in an independent validation study conducted during the 2010-2011 influenza season (c). No significant differences were observed between oCMV− and oCMV+. Green bars = CMV-, yellow bars = CMV+. The age ranges for young and older individuals were 20-30 and 60->89 years, respectively (a); 22-32 (young) and 62->89 (older) years (b) and 19-44 years old (c).

claim_12.claim: Plaque assay analysis of lungs from C57BL/6 mice challenged with influenza A virus 5 weeks after MCMV infection (day 35) showed influenza viral titers were reduced in IAV+ MCMV+ mice compared to IAV+ MCMV− mice at day 7 after IAV challenge (day 42).

sources.quote: Both in early and established latency, we observed better protection against influenza in the MCMV-infected (IAV+ MCMV+) versus the mock-infected (IAV+ MCMV−) mice at day 7 after IAV challenge as seen by the reduced influenza viral titers in the lungs (Fig. 3a and b).

Figure 3. Reduced viral titer and enhanced IAV-specific CD8+ T cell responses in early and established but not long-standing MCMV latency Groups of C57BL/6 mice were mock infected or infected with 4×104 PFU MCMV Smith strain i.p. and challenged with 106 EID50 of IAV ×31 i.n. 5 weeks (early latency) (a and d), 12 weeks (established latency) (b and e) or 9 months (long-standing latency) later (c and f). Seven days after IAV infection, influenza viral titer was determined (upper panel) and IAV-specific T cells were enumerated from the BAL of IAV+ MCMV− (MCMV−) or IAV+ MCMV+ (MCMV+) mice by tetramer staining for NP, PA and PB1-specific responses.

sources.quote: Consistent with this observation, the influenza-specific CD8+ T cell responses against the three major influenza epitopes (DbPA224--233 (PA), KbPB1703-711 (PB1), and DbNP366-374 (NP)) in BAL cells were higher in animals with early and established latency, but not after long-standing latency compared with the mock-infected group (Fig. 3d-f).
